name: sox_ng
why: The Sound eXchange fork, a classic audio Swiss army knife that works well as an instrument and transform tool.

brief.what_it_is: sox_ng is a fork of SoX (Sound eXchange) 14.4.2, a command-line audio Swiss Army knife written mainly in C. It takes audio files (and, with optional libraries, many more formats and video soundtracks) and converts them to other audio file types, applying sound effects and filters during the conversion. It ships as the programs sox_ng, play_ng, rec_ng and soxi_ng, plus the libsox_ng library. The README says it is built on the wider SoX code base, with its own wiki and issue tracker.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the project imports, compares and refines bug fixes and new work from the 50-odd software distributions that package SoX and from the many forks elsewhere, then makes regular releases. It defines sox_ng as "the hard fork of sox-14.4.2 aiming to sanitize SoX".
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. It describes a six-monthly release cadence, with micro releases for bug fixes and minor releases for new features, and says no major, non-backwards-compatible release is planned. Optional features come from libraries: ffmpeg adds about four dozen more formats and video soundtrack extraction, and wget, wget2 or curl let it read URLs as input streams. The README says the binaries behave differently according to their name on Windows (sox.exe, play.exe, rec.exe are the same program).

brief.install_notes: Release source tarballs and Windows zip files are on the Codeberg releases page. Building a release needs make and gcc or clang. Building the git tree also needs autoconf, automake and libtool, then autoreconf -i. Optional modules (LAME, libao, FFTW3, FLAC, libid3tag, libmad, libogg, libopus, libopusfile, libpng, libsndfile, libspeex, libspeexdsp, libvorbis, opencore-amr, twolame, wavpack, ladspa-sdk) are listed with apt, yum and pkg commands for Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/RHEL, and FreeBSD. ffmpeg is optional at runtime. No accounts are needed to install. NetBSD, OpenWRT and Solus have packages on pkgs.org.
brief.standout: It is a deliberate fork that installs under its own names (sox_ng, play_ng, rec_ng, soxi_ng, libsox_ng) so it can sit beside the original sox, and it can also be built to replace sox outright. The project runs a published six-monthly release schedule and keeps a public accounts page.
brief.status: Looks maintained. The Codeberg page shows 4,605 commits, 16 branches, 82 tags and 25 releases. The most recent commit shown is dated 2026-10-18 ("Disable win-utf8-globbing test, failing for wine-related issues"). The README lists a next minor release for 18 November 2026 and a next micro release for 18 February 2027. The page also shows 109 open issues.
brief.caveats: Building from source needs a C toolchain and, for the full feature set, a long list of development libraries. The README says two compiler warnings are normal. The Windows build is distributed as a zip of exes on the releases page. The README does not say what the GPL-style license is beyond a commit message saying it was changed to GPLv2, so check COPYING before relying on it. The Codeberg page shows a notice that LLM-generated content is restricted, which may matter to contributors. The brew caveats field is empty.
